sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.6% a year from FY2017 to FY2026, reaching $67.4 billion [F196][F10].
The path was flat for five years, with revenue of $37.8 billion in FY2017 and $42.4 billion in FY2022, before two step changes [F1][F6].
FY2023 revenue rose 17.7% to $50.0 billion, primarily due to revenue contributions from the Cerner acquisition [D280][F7][P48].

FY2026 revenue rose 17.3% to $67.4 billion on a $9.3 billion increase in cloud and software revenues as customers purchased applications and infrastructure technologies and renewed cloud contracts [D421][F10][P17].
Cloud Infrastructure was the largest latest-year driver, contributing 13.7pp of the 17.3% revenue growth and 26.9% of revenue [D645][D421][D643].
Cloud applications and cloud infrastructure contributed 16% and 84% of constant-currency cloud revenue growth in FY2026 [P17].
The Americas contributed 14.2pp of FY2026 growth and 66.0% of revenue, while Software Support contributed 0.5pp and Software License subtracted 0.8pp [D470][D468][D615][D682].
Operating income grew 16.6% in FY2026 against 17.3% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 29.4% [D422][D421][D442].
Operating costs grew 0.3pp faster than revenue in FY2026, at 17.7% [D443][D436].
Operating margin was 30.6% in FY2026, below the 32.2% window median and well below the 37.6% FY2021 high [F34][D788][D787].
The FY2026 margin slipped 0.2pp: R&D added 1.9pp and other lines subtracted 2.1pp [D433][D444][D445].

The other-line drag reflects a $6.0 billion increase in cloud and software expenses, primarily higher infrastructure expenses, and a $1.5 billion increase in restructuring and other expenses [P19][P11].
Net margin of 25.2% sat 5.4pp below the 30.6% operating margin in FY2026, as interest expense of $4.6 billion and a 28.4% tax rate pulled it down [F54][F34][D832][X92][D407].
Operating cash flow of $32.0 billion was 1.88x net income in FY2026, above the 1.58x window median [F84][D408][D822].
Operating cash flow rose $11.2 billion, primarily due to higher net income adjusted for non-cash charges and favorable working capital, including $4.6 billion of customer prepayments [P6].
Free cash flow was -$23.7 billion, a -35.2% margin, as capex of $55.7 billion reached 82.6% of revenue and 7.30x D&A [F104][D405][F94][D404][D410].
Investing outflows rose $30.1 billion, primarily due to a $34.4 billion increase in capital expenditures [P5].
Net debt reached $97.6 billion in FY2026, net cash of -145.0% of revenue against a -0.5% software peer median, the 0th percentile of six peers [D414][D415][D816][D815].
Total debt rose 39.9% to $129.5 billion, primarily due to $42.7 billion of senior notes issued in FY2026 [D440][D413][P7].
Cash and investments rose 184.7% to $31.9 billion, and the current ratio recovered to 1.12x from the 0.72x FY2024 low [D439][D412][F184][D801].
Buybacks plus dividends of $5.9 billion were 18.4% of the $32.0 billion operating cash flow, and the diluted share count rose 1.7% [D416][F84][D438].
Cash and investments cover 1.3 years of the latest $23.7 billion burn [R1][D419][D418].
The burn is a capex programme rather than an operating loss, but the cushion against it is now thin [D418][F84].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2025 and FY2026, at -0.03x and -1.39x [R2][D362][D409].
Cash conversion has decoupled from earnings, so net income no longer describes the cash the business generates.
Net debt rose for a second year to $97.6 billion, and total debt rose 40% in FY2026 [R3][R4][D414][D413].
Leverage is now the balance-sheet constraint on the cloud build-out, and the $260 billion of additional lease commitments sits outside it [P1].
Whether FY2027 capex falls below the FY2026 $55.7 billion level, in the FY2027 10-K cash flow statement [F94].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers above the -35.2% FY2026 low toward the 26.0% window median, in the FY2027 10-K [D792][D794].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue improves from -145.0% toward the -0.5% peer median, in the FY2027 10-K balance sheet [D415][D816].
